entries.title: Raise a Plan into an Axonometric Model
entries.objective: Connect a supplied two-dimensional plan to its corresponding three-dimensional volumes.
beats: Show the plan flat with a scale reference.
Tilt the view and extrude each polygon to its supplied height.
Hold the completed axonometric model with plan outlines and selected dimensions.
entries.prompt_text: Follow the existing approved contract; if absent, propose one before implementation. Make duration, aspect ratio and FPS configurable. Begin with the approved plan on a flat ground plane, preserving polygon IDs and a visible scale reference. Move the orthographic camera to the supplied axonometric angle while keeping the plan centered. Extrude each polygon vertically to its actual supplied height, revealing one logical group at a time. Retain faint plan outlines beneath the volumes so their origin remains legible. End with a stable model, selected dimensions and a clear unit label. Flag missing heights instead of inventing architectural measurements. Wait for fonts and supplied assets. Derive state from integer frames on one timeline; seed randomness. Perform actual playback and acceptance review only when authorized, and mark unperformed QA NOT VERIFIED.
acceptance: Each volume preserves its source polygon footprint.
Extrusion heights match the supplied units and values.
Orthographic framing keeps the complete required plan readable.
avoid: Inventing dimensions from a visual reference
Changing polygon footprints to create a more attractive skyline

entries.title: Open a Section Through a Layered Object
entries.objective: Reveal supplied internal geometry with a clearly controlled cutting plane.
inputs: Rights-cleared model with actual internal parts
beats: Establish the intact object and cutting-plane marker.
Move the section plane through the model while identifying newly exposed parts.
Hold the selected cross-section with the intact silhouette as a reference.
entries.prompt_text: Follow the existing approved contract; if absent, propose one before implementation. Make duration, aspect ratio and FPS configurable. Place the supplied layered model against a quiet background using a fixed camera that reveals its overall form. Introduce a thin cutting-plane marker before any geometry disappears. Move the plane through the approved path, exposing actual internal parts and adding labels only after they are visible. Use a distinct section-edge treatment so a cut surface cannot be mistaken for the exterior. End at the selected cross-section with a faint intact outline and readable part labels. Report absent interior geometry as an asset gap. Wait for fonts and supplied assets. Derive state from integer frames on one timeline; seed randomness. Perform actual playback and acceptance review only when authorized, and mark unperformed QA NOT VERIFIED.
acceptance: Only real supplied interior parts appear in the cutaway.
Section caps and edges follow the chosen clipping plane.
Part labels point to exposed geometry without hiding the cross-section.
avoid: Fabricating internal structure to fill an empty model
Letting clipping artifacts appear as designed cavities

entries.title: Separate Depth with a Controlled Parallax Move
entries.objective: Show spatial layering through one measured camera translation.
inputs: Rights-cleared foreground, middle and background planes
Camera path and protected content regions
beats: Establish a balanced view of the aligned planes.
Translate the camera laterally so near and far layers separate at different rates.
Settle on the final view with all protected content retained.

Begin with a composed view in which their relationships are understandable, then move the perspective camera laterally along the approved path. Let apparent displacement arise from actual depth and projection rather than separate arbitrary layer speeds. Provide enough artwork beyond the initial crop to prevent exposed edges. End on a stable alternate view with protected content still visible. Treat the construction as layered artwork, not a reconstructed full three-dimensional scene. Wait for fonts and supplied assets. acceptance: Parallax direction and magnitude follow the declared depths and camera path.

avoid: Claiming missing viewpoints exist in flat source artwork

entries.title: Trace a Route Across an Isometric Network
entries.objective: Explain a connected route while preserving topology and legible waypoints.
beats: Establish the network and starting waypoint.
Advance a route marker along connected edges, pausing at approved stops.
Hold the entire completed route with start, destination and stop sequence visible.

Draw the supplied network in a fixed isometric view with one unobtrusive ground reference. Keep inactive edges muted while the chosen route is progressively revealed. Move a marker only along the supplied connected edges and pause at each approved stop long enough for its label to settle. Place labels in an overlay rail when geometry becomes crowded. End with the full route, start and destination visible together. Clearly identify whether edge lengths represent real distances or a schematic arrangement. Wait for fonts and supplied assets. Derive state from integer frames on one timeline; seed randomness. Perform actual playback and acceptance review only when authorized, and mark unperformed QA NOT VERIFIED.
acceptance: The marker follows connected edges in the correct order.
Waypoint labels match the supplied route.
The distance interpretation is explicit and consistent.
avoid: Jumping between unconnected nodes to shorten the animation
Implying geographic accuracy from a schematic isometric layout

entries.title: Change Coordinate Frames Without Moving the Point
entries.objective: Distinguish a fixed world-space point from its coordinates in changing reference frames.
inputs: World point and two valid coordinate transforms
beats: Show the point and first reference frame.
Introduce the second frame and transform the displayed coordinates.
Hold both coordinate descriptions beside the same unchanged world-space point.

Place one clearly marked point in a simple three-dimensional scene with a fixed world grid. Show the first coordinate frame and its numeric description of that point. Introduce the second approved frame through its translation and rotation while keeping the world point stationary. Update coordinate labels from the actual inverse transform rather than moving the point to match the numbers. End with both axis triads and both coordinate descriptions visible, using distinct frame labels and consistent units. Wait for fonts and supplied assets. Derive state from integer frames on one timeline; seed randomness. Perform actual playback and acceptance review only when authorized, and mark unperformed QA NOT VERIFIED.
acceptance: The world-space point remains fixed throughout the frame change.
Both coordinate descriptions agree under the supplied transforms.
Axis handedness and units are explicit.
avoid: Moving the point while claiming only the reference frame changed
Mixing local and world coordinates in one label

entries.title: Explain a Mirror Reflection with Ray Geometry

Add angle arcs in the plane of incidence and label them under the chosen convention. A small secondary preview may show a rendered reflection, but the ray diagram remains the explanatory focus. acceptance: The reflected direction follows the geometric reflection rule.

avoid: Measuring one angle from the surface and the other from the normal

Fade or relocate labels according to the declared policy when features become occluded; do not let leader lines imply an exposed surface that is actually hidden. acceptance: Each leader line remains attached to its actual model anchor.

entries.title: Reassemble a Point Cloud Through Stable Correspondence
entries.objective: Transform between supplied point configurations while preserving identifiable correspondences.
inputs: Equal-sized source and target point sets
beats: Establish the source form with a few tracked point IDs.
Move points along their assigned paths while retaining the overall mass.
Resolve the target form and hold the tracked correspondences.

Render the supplied source point set as restrained instanced marks in a fixed spatial frame. Highlight a small number of stable IDs so the viewer can understand correspondence. Move each point toward its assigned target along the approved path, using a shared time parameter and a controlled stagger only where specified. Keep the camera simple enough that the transformation itself remains the subject. End with the exact target point set and selected IDs visible. Flag unequal point counts or missing correspondences before implementation. Wait for fonts and supplied assets. Derive state from integer frames on one timeline; seed randomness. Perform actual playback and acceptance review only when authorized, and mark unperformed QA NOT VERIFIED.
acceptance: Every source point maps to the assigned target identity.
The ending reaches the exact supplied target coordinates.

avoid: Randomly rematching points on every render

Hold the aligned view long enough to read the target. If authorized, finish with a small offset that reveals the construction while retaining a final reference thumbnail of the resolved image.
